property_summary: After initialization, SetMinSum must not change MinSum; the reference reverts any call after initialization leaving MinSum unchanged, while the buggy version updates MinSum before reverting.
After a call to SetMinSum reverts, the stored MinSum must equal its value before the call; the buggy contract updates MinSum before reverting, violating this post‑revert invariance.
After a revert on SetMinSum, the stored MinSum must equal the value it had before the call; the buggy contract updates MinSum before reverting, violating this post‑revert invariance.
After initialization, any call to SetMinSum must revert and leave MinSum unchanged; the buggy mutant updates MinSum before reverting, so a reverted call changes MinSum.
For any input, after a reverted call to SetMinSum the value of MinSum must equal the value it had before the call; the buggy mutant updates MinSum before reverting, so a reverted call changes MinSum.

After any sequence of calls, the stored MinSum value must remain equal to the last value passed to SetMinSum, but the buggy version allows a reentrant call to overwrite it during a reentrant Collect, resulting in a different final MinSum.

After a call to SetMinSum completes, the MinSum value must be at least as large as the value passed to that call, but the buggy version allows a reentrant call to overwrite it with a smaller value, breaking this monotonicity.

After a successful call to SetMinSum from a caller that is not a contract, MinSum must equal the value passed to that call, but the bug allows a reentrant call from a malicious contract during Collect to overwrite MinSum with a different value.

After a successful call to SetMinSum, MinSum must equal the value passed to that call, unless a later top-level call changes it; the buggy non-reentrant modifier allows a reentrant call during Collect to overwrite MinSum with a different value before the original SetMinSum completes.

After a successful call to SetMinSum, MinSum must equal the value passed to that call, assuming no other top-level call to SetMinSum intervenes; the buggy non-reentrant modifier allows a reentrant call during Collect to overwrite MinSum with a different value before SetMinSum completes.

After the first call to SetMinSum, the reference contract allows a second call to SetMinSum to succeed, while the buggy contract causes a second call to SetMinSum to always revert due to the lock being permanently set.

After successful SetLogFile call, the Log state variable address must exactly equal the LogFile address derived from the argument address; the mutant sets it to address(0) regardless of input, breaking this equality.
